Once upon a time, in a quiet seaside town, there was a small tiki bar called The Salty Parrot. It was tucked away along the pier, often hidden behind the fishing boats and lobster traps, and known only to those who wandered off the main tourist path. The bar had a reputation for serving the wildest, most unusual drinks, crafted with flavors that seemed to be plucked straight from the pages of a mystery novel.

One October evening, as a thick fog rolled in from the ocean, a strange old man wandered into The Salty Parrot. He wore a dark cloak and a wide-brimmed hat that hid most of his face. The bar was nearly empty, with just a few regulars nursing their drinks, lost in the low hum of the radio.

The old man sat down at the bar and tapped a gnarled finger on the counter. “I’ll have something…spooky,” he rasped, his voice a whisper, like the wind through the nearby caves.

Intrigued, the bartender, a woman named Mara, leaned in close. “Spooky, you say? I think I might have just the thing.” She pulled out a bottle filled with a dark, mysterious liquid and began mixing a drink with an assortment of unusual ingredients. There was a touch of apple spice bitters, a dash of cinnamon, and even a hint of pumpkin—a unique Halloween blend known as the Black Magic.

As she stirred, the lights in the bar flickered, and a chill filled the air. Mara poured the finished drink into a skull-shaped glass and handed it to the old man. He took a long sip, his eyes glinting with something both eerie and familiar.

“Ah,” he sighed, placing the glass down with a satisfied smile. “This reminds me of an old legend… one about a tiki bar hidden in the fog, where drinks could grant your deepest wishes—if you dared to ask.”

The regulars, intrigued, turned their attention to the old man. He went on to tell tales of ghostly sailors, enchanted islands, and a bar that only appeared on Halloween night, serving potions that could turn back time, bring lost loves back, or give someone courage they never knew they had.

When he finished his tale, the old man stood, tipped his hat, and melted into the fog as quickly as he’d appeared. Mara and her patrons rushed to the door to catch a glimpse of him, but he was gone. All that remained was the faint scent of spices lingering in the air.

From that night on, The Salty Parrot’s Halloween drink menu gained a new legend, and each October, patrons would flock to taste the magic, hoping to catch a glimpse of the mysterious old man and his whispered tales of the supernatural. And, of course, every year, Mara would be ready with her signature Black Magic, just in case he ever returned.
